title: Structural and functional basis for internal derangement of the temporomandibular joint: a histological investigation
html: Recent years have seen increased interest in treating temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. Much therapy, both surgical and non-surgical, has been based on assumptions of anatomy largely defined by gross dissection studies with insufficient level of detail to illustrate its intricacy. This study defines the insertion of the superior head of the lateral pterygoid (SLP) muscle. Twenty-five cadaveric joints were retrieved en bloc and sectioned parasagittally. Histologic sections were taken every 100–200 µm, stained using the Masson trichrome technique, and examined for muscular insertion.
